summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of spinal cord injury from a gunshot wound, paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and chronic indwelling Foley catheter was admitted for persistent bilateral flank pain lasting two weeks. She denied fever but reported shaking chills and foul-smelling urine. Initial labs showed mild leukocytosis, which improved on repeat testing. Urine culture grew Escherichia coli and Enterococcus species, and she was treated with cefpodoxime for a 14-day course based on prior sensitivities. Her pain was only partially attributed to urinary infection, and her Foley catheter was changed during the stay. She remained afebrile with stable vital signs. Cocaine use was confirmed on admission, though she showed no withdrawal. She was discharged home with antibiotics, a short course of pain medication, and instructions to follow up with her new primary care provider for culture results and chronic pain evaluation.
